3. The respondent herein is a company engaged in providing trade facilitation services, including procurement, logistics, warehousing, inspection, valuation, and quality testing in relation to commodities.
The petitioner herein is a company engaged in the business of sugar trading.

At the request of the petitioner herein, the parties entered into a Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) and a Statement of Work (SOW) dated 26.04.2017, whereby the respondent herein agreed to procure sugar on behalf of the petitioner herein in accordance with specifications to be provided by the petitioner herein.

sentences.text: Under the TFA, the petitioner herein was required to specify the quantity, quality, source, delivery timelines, and other particulars of the commodity through the SOW.

The agreement defined "commodity consideration" to include the landed cost of the commodity, procurement charges,
warehousing charges, delayed charges, and all other costs and fees payable by the petitioner herein.
It was expressly agreed that title in the commodity would pass to the petitioner herein only upon full payment of the commodity consideration.

In the event of non-payment or failure to take delivery,
the respondent herein was entitled to exercise a lien over the goods, dispose of the same, and appropriate the sale proceeds towards outstanding dues.
The respondent herein was also entitled to levy storage and delayed charges and to provide warehousing services where required.
5. Pursuant to the SOW, which was valid until 25.03.2018, the respondent herein was required to procure up to 5500 MT of sugar and arrange for warehousing.

The terms further stipulated that the petitioner herein would inspect the goods within one day of their arrival at the warehouse and confirm acceptance of quality and quantity, failing which no dispute in that regard could be raised later.
The respondent herein was not responsible for any damage occurring after delivery to the warehouse, save for arranging insurance.

In the event the petitioner herein failed to lift the goods within the stipulated period, the respondent herein was entitled to sell the same upon giving prior notice and adjust the proceeds against its dues.

arbitrariness, or fundamental illegality going to the root of the matter, none of which were demonstrated in the present case.

sentences.text: Both Counsels for parties addressed a lengthy argument qua their respective stand to oppose or support the Award.

22. Before adverting to the merits of the challenge, it is necessary to recapitulate the well-settled principles governing the scope and ambit of judicial interference with arbitral awards under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

23. The Supreme Court, in Associate Builders (supra), authoritatively held that an arbitral award can be set aside only if it is contrary to: (i) the fundamental policy of Indian law; (ii) the interest of India; (iii) justice or morality; or (iv) is patently illegal.
It was further clarified that re-appreciation of evidence, correction of factual errors, or substitution of the court's view for that of the arbitrator is impermissible.
OMP (COMM)-1/2025 PROGRESSIVE SALES PVT LTD. vs. NORTH END FOODS MARKETING PVT LTD DoD 30.03.2026 Pages No. 10 of 24.

sentences.text: Subsequently, in Ssangyong Engineering (supra), the Supreme Court significantly narrowed the contours of "public policy" post the 2015 Amendment and held that interference is permissible only when the award suffers from perversity, patent illegality apparent on the face of the award, or contravention of the fundamental policy of Indian law.

25. In MMTC Ltd. v. Vedanta Ltd. AIR 2019 SC 1168 and in Delhi Airport Metro Express Pvt. Ltd. v.
DMRC, (2022) 1 SCC 131, the Supreme Court further cautioned that Section 34 does not permit the court to act as a court of appeal and reassess evidence, and interference is justified only where the arbitrator's view is one which no reasonable person would take, or where vital evidence has been ignored, resulting in perversity.

Seen in the light of aforesaid precedents, it is crystal clear that the court under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, cannot sit in appeal, review merits, or modify an award by Progressive Sales Pvt Ltd vs North End Foods Marketing Pvt Ltd on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117751876/

30. In the present petition, therefore, the scope of judicial scrutiny is confined to a singular and well-defined question, namely, whether the impugned arbitral award dated 05.10.2024 suffers from any infirmity warranting interference under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996, on the grounds urged by the petitioner.

31. Perusal of the impugned award shows that the Ld. Arbitrator, while adjudicating the dispute,
noted that the respondent herein had taken inconsistent stands regarding the condition of the 402 MT of sugar - initially asserting that the stock was damaged and pursuing claims with the warehouse and insurer, and subsequently taking a "U-turn" by claiming that the sugar was in a fit condition and calling upon the petitioner herein to lift the goods within a stipulated time, failing which the same would be auctioned.

The Ld. Arbitrator also took note of the disputes surrounding inspection of the goods, the petitioner's contention that it was denied an opportunity to inspect, and the challenges raised to the respondent's evidence, including the report relied OMP (COMM)-1/2025 PROGRESSIVE SALES PVT LTD. vs. NORTH END FOODS MARKETING PVT LTD DoD 30.03.2026 Pages No. 12 of upon to assert that the sugar was not damaged.

On this basis, the Ld.
Arbitrator held that the conduct of the respondent herein was not entirely consistent or free from doubt, particularly in relation to its claims for additional charges and interest.
Ld. Arbitrator also noted that Clause 39 and 40 of the TFA was not applicable to the present dispute.

32. However, the Ld. Arbitrator proceeded on the reasoning that, irrespective of such inconsistencies, the petitioner herein had failed to lift the sugar despite notice and that the goods were ultimately auctioned by the respondent herein.

Treating the petitioner herein as liable for the consequences of non-lifting, the Ld. Arbitrator held that the respondent herein was entitled to recover the difference between the auction price and the claimed market price, quantified at Rs.
45,78,267/-.

At the same time, due to the respondent's own conduct, the Ld. Arbitrator denied the remaining claims, including delayed charges and interest, and thus partly allowed the claim only to the limited extent of the said price difference.
33. Respondent herein did not prefer to challenge the award to the extent it refused other claims of respondent herein.
Hence, findings against it has become final.

34. The Ld. Arbitrator recorded the following adverse findings against the respondent herein:
i.

The respondent herein took mutually inconsistent and contradictory stands regarding the condition of 402 MT OMP (COMM)-1/2025 PROGRESSIVE SALES PVT LTD. vs. NORTH END FOODS MARKETING PVT LTD DoD 30.03.2026 Pages No. 13 of sugar - first claiming it was damaged, and later asserting it was fit for sale.

The respondent herein wrongfully denied the petitioner herein an opportunity to inspect the goods, on the incorrect ground that the sugar had already been auctioned.
iv. The respondent's assertion regarding prior auction was factually incorrect, as evidence showed that the sale occurred at a later point of time.
v. The respondent's ledger entries was not reliable and thus it failed to substantiate its monetary claims, including delayed charges and ledger entries, which lacked proper basis.
vi. The contractual provisions (Clauses 39 & 40) relied upon by the respondent herein were found to be inapplicable in the facts of the case.
vii. Due to its conduct, the respondent herein was held not entitled to delayed charges, other charges, or interest.

35. Be that as it may, perusal of the Award shows that Ld. Arbitrator, while framing the scope of adjudication, categorically held that the only question arising for consideration between the parties was whether the 402 MT of sugar was damaged or not.

Having so confined the controversy, it was incumbent upon the Ld. Arbitrator to return a clear and reasoned finding on the said issue,
particularly in view of the fact that the respective claims and defences of the parties were fundamentally premised on the condition of the said stock.

However, perusal of the Award OMP (COMM)-1/2025 PROGRESSIVE SALES PVT LTD. vs. NORTH END FOODS MARKETING PVT LTD DoD 30.03.2026 Pages No. 14 of reveals that no definitive finding has been rendered on this core issue.

36. The Ld. Arbitrator has noticed the contradictory stands of the respondent herein - initially asserting that the sugar was damaged and pursuing an insurance claim on that basis, and subsequently asserting that the same was in a fit condition - but has failed to adjudicate upon which of the two stands is to be accepted.
In the absence of such determination, the conclusion fastening liability upon the petitioner herein becomes unsustainable, being disconnected from the very issue identified for adjudication.
37. It is further evident that the Award suffers from internal inconsistency and non-application of mind.

While the Ld. Arbitrator has, on account of the inconsistent conduct of the respondent herein,
denied its claim towards delayed charges and interest, he has nevertheless proceeded to allow the claim towards the alleged difference in price of the sugar without reconciling the same contradictions.

Once the conduct of the respondent herein in taking mutually inconsistent stands with respect to the condition of the goods was found to be unreliable, the Ld. Arbitrator could not have selectively accepted a part of the respondent's case without any cogent reasoning.
Such selective acceptance of evidence, in the absence of any rational basis, renders the findings perverse and legally untenable.

However, from the evidence on record, including the cross-examination of the respondent's witness, it emerges that the alleged sale took place at a later point in time, thereby casting serious doubt on the respondent's stand.
The denial of inspection, in such circumstances, assumes significance as it directly impacts the determination of the condition of the goods and the fairness of the alleged resale.
The Ld. Arbitrator has noted these facts but has failed to draw any inference therefrom or to adjudicate upon their effect, thereby ignoring vital evidence.

39. Equally, the petitioner's specific case that it had attempted to lift the goods by sending trucks in or about February 2018, but was prevented from doing so, has not been adjudicated upon by the Ld.
Arbitrator.
This plea, if established, would have a direct bearing on the question as to whether there was any breach on the part of the petitioner at all.
The Ld. Arbitrator has merely recorded this contention in passing but has not returned any finding as to its correctness or otherwise.
The non-consideration of such a material plea goes to the root of the matter and vitiates the Award.

40. Further, the Award is silent on the aspect that the respondent herein, after having consistently represented that the goods were damaged and pursuing remedies on that basis, suddenly took a OMP (COMM)-1/2025 PROGRESSIVE SALES PVT LTD. vs. NORTH END FOODS MARKETING PVT LTD DoD 30.03.2026 Pages No. 16 of complete volte-face by asserting that the goods were fit for consumption and calling upon the petitioner herein to lift the same within an unreasonably short period, failing which the goods would be disposed of. The Ld. Arbitrator has neither examined whether, in view of this abrupt change in position, any reasonable opportunity ought to have been afforded to the petitioner herein to verify and lift the goods, nor whether the subsequent disposal of the goods was in accordance with the contractual stipulations and principles of fairness. The absence of any finding on this aspect renders the conclusion regarding the petitioner's liability for the alleged loss wholly unsupported.
